analysis: The PR changes only the CI route workflow (.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml), a changelog entry and developer docs. It does not touch provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, encryption, caches or fan helper code, so I found no direct effect on A-001..A-020 or TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013/014. Reviewed behavior: (1) The route client adds the header X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 at head line 169. It carries no secret and does not widen the request body. (2) At head lines 200-202 the expected runner label array now has -run-<RUN_ID> appended to its last label, after any size suffix. A plane decision is accepted only if its runs_on equals this array exactly (head line 207). Anything else falls back to the existing fallback label. This is a tightening: the plane cannot inject arbitrary labels, and an idle runner from an older run cannot match a newer run's job. RUN_ID is validated as numeric (head line 154) before any request is sent. The jq --arg run_id receives RUN_ID as a string, so there is no injection risk. When the routing reply is not requested or the reason is a fallback, $reply is /dev/null and RUN_ID is still defined from the env, so the jq expression is safe. (3) The fork-PR guard (head line 146), https-only check, size and time limits, and the clean sanitizer for plane text are unchanged. Docs and changelog match the code. They say retries keep the original route output, which is a property of the GitHub Actions outputs, not something this PR changes. Remaining unverified contract: whether the external sandbox plane and its runners actually honor the run-scoped labels. That is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence. A mismatch only degrades to the fallback runner (availability and cost), not a security regression. No findings.
